clue.text: Inform, ___ but when (the Fourth of July?)

parts.note: the blank completes the stock phrase 'not if, but when', so it stands for the words NOT IF

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the word July is taken, a pun on the American holiday

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank about when American Independence Day falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Fourth of July' looks like the holiday, but it asks for the fourth letter of July. The blank completes 'not if, but when'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone formally is to give them notice of something, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Writer rising against fine Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: V for versus means against
OK means fine
Oban is a port town in western Scotland

explanation.surface: An author's rise sets them against a pleasant Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The rising applies to all three pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir, the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita, was a writer.

clue.text: The whole pit express disapproval over it

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound expressing disapproval

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upwards, so reversed

explanation.surface: The audience in the pit all tutting at a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The pit is the orchestra pit, so 'the whole pit' is the full orchestra, which this musical direction asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction that all the orchestra plays together, the whole band in the pit.

clue.text: Sell-out crowd gives a good hand

definitions.meaning: a theatre with every seat sold
in poker, three of a kind plus a pair

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a packed theatre and a strong poker hand of three and two.

clue.text: Pop art isn't a movement

indicators.note: to pop something is to burst it, so the letters of the following words break apart and re-form

explanation.surface: An art-world quip that Pop Art doesn't count as a real artistic movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop art' reads as the art style, but 'Pop' bursts the letters of 'art isn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage or conveyance from one place to another is a kind of movement.

clue.text: Create large solution of sweet liquid

indicators.note: a solution dissolves things, so the letters are dissolved and remixed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Instructions to make a big solution of sweet liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' suggests a liquid, but it rearranges CREATE with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup or molasses, the thick sweet liquid from sugar refining.

clue.text: Record-breaking compound (black)

indicators.note: breaking into something gets inside it, so the colour letter goes into the compound

parts.note: alum is a chemical compound, a double sulphate
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A record-breaking chemical compound, with black in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-breaking' looks like one adjective, but 'Record' is the definition and 'breaking' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP or set of tracks issued together is a record.

clue.text: Wise guy graduate wearing scarlet shift

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so the degree goes inside the rearranged letters
a shift is a dress, but also a change, so the letters move

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A clever graduate wearing a scarlet dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a dress worn by the graduate, but it scrambles SCARLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all who shows off their cleverness, a sarcastic wise guy.

clue.text: Shot over target with it

indicators.note: the attempt goes over and around the aim, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a try
an end is a target or goal

explanation.surface: A shot that goes over the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' reads like 'along with it', but it is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable and up to date is what 'with it' means in slang.

clue.text: Spoiler on vehicle lawyer left behind

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the letter for left goes at the end

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A spoiler on a vehicle a lawyer left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiler' suggests a car's aerofoil, but it means someone who wrecks things.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wilfully damages property spoils it.

clue.text: For example, Maggie Thatcher (British prime minister) once admitted a wrong

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the pair of letters is placed inside the name

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the Labour prime minister of Britain from 1945 to 1951
X is the cross a teacher marks against a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A remark that a former prime minister once confessed to an error.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was Britain's famously formidable prime minister, so she is an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering, combative woman is called this, and Thatcher was often given the label.

clue.text: Jewellery not allowed for 2

indicators.note: the word 'not' tells us to strip away the synonym of 'allowed' from the piece of jewellery

parts.note: a bracelet is a piece of jewellery worn on the wrist
let means allowed, as in 'let in'

explanation.surface: A rule that some jewellery is banned for two people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bare number 2: a pair of game birds is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of things, especially shot game birds, is a common term for two.

clue.text: Sent back hotpot dumpling

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so these letters are read from the end

parts.note: split as hot plus pot: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps, and to pot a snooker ball is to sink it

explanation.surface: A diner returning a dish of stew to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hotpot' looks like the stew, but it splits into hot (H) and pot (SINK, as in snooker).
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish baked or fried pastry filled with potato or meat, a kind of dumpling.

clue.text: Killed many animals turning them inside out

indicators.note: the reversed animals are placed inside the synonym for 'out'

parts.note: out, as in out of fashion, means dated

indicators.note: turning the animals round makes us read their letters backwards

parts.note: mice are small animals

explanation.surface: A lurid report of creatures being killed and turned inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside out' looks like a single phrase but splits: 'inside' is the container signal and 'out' gives DATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally to kill one in ten, the word now means to kill a large proportion of a group.

clue.text: Provide food offcut to be stuffed in bottle

indicators.note: stuffing one thing into another puts it inside, so the scrambled letters go into the bottle

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

indicators.note: food that is off has gone bad, signalling the letters of the next word are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: feed people by stuffing a bottle with trimmings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offcut' reads as one word for a scrap, but it splits: 'off' is the anagram signal working on the three letters after it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, the word means to supply with provisions or food, an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Cold fish skin used for wrapping

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps
ling is a long fish of the cod family
a film is a thin skin, as on custard

explanation.surface: A cold fish with its skin used for wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin transparent plastic sheet that sticks to itself, used to wrap food.

clue.text: See about investment return with little effort

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bishop's seat goes around the other piece

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in England, the seat (see) of a bishop

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the investment's letters are read backwards

parts.note: an ISA is a British tax-free savings account, an Individual Savings Account

explanation.surface: Advice to check how an investment's return can be had effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings scheme; Ely is a cathedral city, so a 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with little effort is doing it without difficulty, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Poll covering sweet and sour cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poll that covers sweet and sour cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' suggests a vote, but it is an old word for the head, so the definition is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof hat with a broad back brim is a covering for the head, poll being the head.

clue.text: Flicks coins inside, heads on reverse — so be it

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters
reverse means backwards, so the prayer word is read the other way

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer, meaning so be it

explanation.surface: Someone flicking coins and calling heads with resignation about the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flicks', 'coins', 'heads' and 'reverse' all suggest tossing a coin, but 'Flicks' is the definition (films).
explanation.definitionFit: The flicks is British slang for the films, or the picture house that shows them.

clue.text: Mammal rounds on another one performing in circus

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
to round on is to turn, so the mammal's letters are turned backwards

parts.note: the orca, the killer whale, is a mammal
another mammal, the bat

explanation.surface: A mammal turns round on another one performing in a circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' gives a second mammal, the BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who performs tumbling and trapeze feats in a circus ring.

clue.text: Rider embraces wildcat strikes

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so the cat goes inside the rider's letters

parts.note: a rider is an addition to a document, like a PS (postscript)
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a wild cat

explanation.surface: A horseman holding a wildcat as it lashes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildcat strikes' suggests industrial action, but 'strikes' is the definition and 'wildcat' the ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring suddenly on prey is to attack, so the verb means strikes.

clue.text: Doorman flicks old style penny

indicators.note: to flick is to flip, so the old-style word is flipped round backwards

parts.note: retro means in an old style

explanation.surface: A doorman flicking an old-style penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old style penny' suggests the predecimal D, but it splits into RETRO and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel or college gatekeeper who minds the door.

clue.text: Mediates, when spite erupts between opponents

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go between the two players

parts.note: S and N, South and North, are opposing partnerships in bridge

indicators.note: something erupting bursts out in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone intervenes when spite flares up between rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South are opposite sides in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene in a dispute is to mediate.

clue.text: A mountain, a river and a desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert

explanation.surface: A list of geographical features: a mountain, river and desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is a verb, not a landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish peak where Noah's Ark is said to have come to rest.

clue.text: Union official behind arresting core Republican

indicators.note: arresting means seizing and holding, so the bottom holds the other letters inside

parts.note: the rear is the behind
the gist is the core of a matter

explanation.surface: A trade union official at the back seizing a key Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: This official records births and marriages and conducts civil weddings, so presides over a union.

clue.text: Material influenced broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so we take what the word sounds like

parts.note: to sway someone is to influence them

explanation.surface: Material that has influenced a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather with a napped surface, a material used for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Permit energy to be delivered up front after surge in current

indicators.note: being delivered to the front means the letter is moved to the start

parts.note: to agree to something is to permit it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A notice about permitting an energy delivery during a power surge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surge in current' suggests electricity, but it means a tidal surge in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal bore, a wave surging up a river against its current, as on the Trent.

clue.text: Class right to have vital transmitter outside

indicators.note: the transmitter sits outside, wrapping round the letter

parts.note: a gene transmits hereditary traits, vital to life

explanation.surface: Class rights to a vital transmitter outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A category or kind, especially of art or writing, is a class.

clue.text: Euros exchanged for last of old money flowing through Europe

indicators.note: exchanging one thing for another swaps it out, so a letter is replaced
only the last letter of the money word is exchanged

parts.note: rhino is dated British slang for money
E is the abbreviation for Euros

explanation.surface: Euros swapped for the last of someone's old currency on a trip through Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old money' suggests old currencies, but it is RHINO, old slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A great river that flows through Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands.

clue.text: First milk produced painful swellings

definitions.meaning: the first milk a cow gives after calving, rich in antibodies
the lumps left where bees have stung

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both colostrum from a cow and the swellings from bee stings.

clue.text: First music septet played was Stormy Weather

indicators.note: music played can be arranged differently, so these letters are rearranged
the first letter of the word music is taken

explanation.surface: A septet's opening number was the jazz standard Stormy Weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Stormy Weather is a song title, but here it simply defines a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm, which is stormy weather.

clue.text: Sort of scan applied to head of hapless character

parts.note: MR stands for magnetic resonance, as in an MR or MRI scan
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A scan being applied to someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the bumbling comedy character played by Rowan Atkinson.
explanation.definitionFit: The fumbling, accident-prone figure from the TV comedy is the archetypal hapless character.
